---
title: "Storage basins"
---

A Basin in a regional model stands for a whole network of waterways.
To represent that water does not all flow at once, most Basins come in a pair, with the same area:

- a _doorgaand_ Basin for the flowing water, on the main route through the area, and
- a _bergend_ Basin for the stagnant water, in the ditches and small watercourses.

Precipitation, evaporation and groundwater reach them differently, see [Forcing](forcing.qmd#sec-budgets).
In the coupled model, about 9800 of the 20 200 Basins are bergend, and 2300 are hoofdwater, the main water system and the KRW water bodies.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "The two ways in which a storage Basin connects to its doorgaand Basin."
flowchart LR
  subgraph drain["Drains only"]
    b1["bergend"] -->|"TabulatedRatingCurve<br>Van der Gaast"| d1["doorgaand"]
  end
  subgraph both["Can also be supplied"]
    b2["bergend"] <-->|ManningResistance| d2["doorgaand"]
  end
```

## Gravity controlled models

`pipeline/05_add_bergend.py` adds a storage Basin to each Basin with `ribasim_nl.berging.VdGaastBerging`, from the rasters of the LHM and of Van der Gaast.
It drains through a TabulatedRatingCurve.

In the supply areas of `verwerkt/sturing/aanvoergebieden.gpkg` with `meta_aanvoer` true, the storage Basin connects with a ManningResistance instead, so it can also be supplied.
A Basin counts as supplied if at least half of its area lies in a supply area, see `ribasim_nl.berging.supply_area_basin_ids`.

## Level controlled models

The [profile generation](profile-generation.qmd) derives both profiles from the hydro-objects and the BGT, and adds the storage Basins, always with a ManningResistance.
Without any usable profile, the Basin keeps one Basin with a fallback profile.
